html:
The Gayiri, also known as the Kairi and by many other spellings, are an Aboriginal Australian people of central Queensland, in the country around today's Springsure and the Nogoa River.

In October 1861 nineteen settlers, among them the squatter Horatio Wills, were killed at Cullin-la-ringo station, newly taken up on their land. Gayiri men are generally named as the attackers. This Cullin-la-ringo massacre was the largest killing of settlers by Aboriginal people in Australian history, and the revenge raids by settlers and the Native Police killed far more Gayiri. Horatio's son Tom Wills, a founder of Australian rules football, survived because he was away.

Their neighbours were the Wangan, Gabalbara and Garingbal.
sum: The Gayiri, also known as the Kairi and by many other spellings, are an Aboriginal Australian people of central Queensland, in the country around today's Springsure and the Nogoa River.
